fix.s:
Consider the following statements about Pulakesin II's eastern campaign:
1. He conquered Kosala and Kalinga before marching to Vengi.
2. After taking Vengi he defeated the Durjayas and then turned against the Pallava Mahendravarman I.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
fix.x: Both are correct: Pulakesin II conquered Kosala and Kalinga, marched to Vengi, defeated the Durjayas and then fought the Pallava Mahendravarman I. In 617 the Satara inscription records his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana as viceroy of Vengi.

restore.why: key fixed: notes say mother goddess = Hariti, not Kushmandini (a Jain yakshi)

fix.x: The Eastern Chalukyas called themselves Haritiputras and their mother goddess was Hariti (APPSC G2 2019); Kushmandini is a Jain yakshi. Kalyanakaraka is Ugradityacharya's medical treatise, not a Shaiva school, and the leading Jain centre was Potlacheruvu.

restore.why: ambiguity removed: Vesara option replaced since notes also call the Vengi school Vesara

fix.x: The Eastern Chalukyas mainly followed a Dravida-based style (Dravidian vimana), blending Pallava and Badami Chalukya influences with local Andhra features; this tradition is called the Vengi School (also described as Vesara/Chalukya).

restore.why: key fixed: notes say Anavota Reddy shifted the capital to Kondavidu

fix.x: Anavota Reddy (c. 1355) shifted the Reddi capital from Addanki to the fortified Kondavidu; Prolaya Vemareddy, the founder, ruled from Addanki.

restore.why: reign dates corrected to 1070-1122 per notes

o: He was killed at Koppam while riding an elephant.
He was the founder who captured Thanjavur in 850 CE.
He defeated Pallava Aparajita and annexed Tondaimandalam.
He was the first ruler of the Chalukya-Chola line and ruled from 1070 to 1122 CE.
fix.x: Kulottunga I was the first ruler of the Chalukya-Chola line (1070-1122 CE). Rajadhiraja I died at Koppam, Vijayalaya took Thanjavur, and Aditya I defeated Aparajita and annexed Tondaimandalam.

restore.why: two right options removed: Agastya is Vidyanatha, replaced with Palkuriki Somanatha

fix.x: Vidyanatha (identified with Agastya), court poet of Prataparudra II, wrote Prataparudra Yashobhushanam (APPSC G2 2011 key). Ekamranatha wrote Prataparudra Charitramu, Palkuriki Somanatha was a Veerashaiva poet, and Sakalya Malla is not credited with this work.

restore.why: key fixed: notes give 77 Nayankaras (72 = Niyogas)

fix.s: How many Nayankaras were there in the Kakatiya kingdom?
fix.x: There were 77 Nayankaras, each guarding a fort; together they controlled one-fourth of the land. 72 is the number of Niyogas (central departments) and 12 the Ayagars of a village.

restore.why: stem fixed: notes say Veerashaivism was the popular religion of the Reddi period; Pasupata stayed popular into it

fix.s: Which Shaiva sect, the oldest of them, remained popular into the Reddi period and declined under Vijayanagara?
fix.x: Pasupata, the oldest Shaiva sect (founded by Lakulisa), stayed popular into the Reddi period, when the kings patronised it, and declined under Vijayanagara. Kapalikas were its offshoot; Kalamukha was a separate sect.

restore.why: second wrong option fixed: Rudramadevi succeeded in 1262 per notes

o: Rudra Deva ascended the throne in 1158
Ganapatideva shifted the capital to Warangal by 1254
Pratapa Rudra ascended the throne before Rudramadevi
fix.x: Pratapa Rudra came to the throne in 1296, after Rudramadevi (1262); the other three statements are correct.
